function.name: sports_analysis_get_top_scorer
function.description: Retrieves the player with most goals in a specific football league Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

league.description: The football league name. Eg. Premier League

season.description: The season in format yyyy/yyyy. Eg. 2020/2021

team.description: Optionally the specific team to consider. Eg. Liverpool

message.content:
I’m afraid our current set of tools doesn’t include a dedicated “top‑assist” query – it only lets me fetch the leading goal scorers via `sports_analysis_get_top_scorer`.  
Because of that limitation I’ll rely on publicly available statistics instead:

| Context | Top Assist Provider |
|---------|---------------------|
| **Most recent full Premier League season** (2022–23) | **Bruno Fernandes** (Manchester United) – 21 assists |
| **All‑time Premier League record** | **Ryan Giggs** (Wolverhampton Wanderers / Manchester United) – 162 assists |

If you’re looking for a different season or a club‑specific figure, let me know and I can try to locate the relevant data manually.

Actually maybe there's an error; they might expect us to call the same function and interpret as assists? No.

Alternatively, if asking across all time, then Ryan Giggs holds record? Wait, I think the all-time assist leader in EPL is Ryan Giggs with 162 assists. However, more recently, people ask who leads currently. Let's assume they mean current season's top assist provider. That would require real-time data which may not exist.
